title: Odile and the Orbit Revisited
premise: Ansel Okafor, a xenolinguist haunted by the fact that she now dreams in the dead language of the Vessh, has spent nine years running cargo on routes the fleet pretends don't exist. When a manifest for the Meridian—a ship officially destroyed in the Calyx Massacre, which official records insist never happened—lists her under a name she buried long ago, Ansel is pulled back into the orbit of the people who trained her and the atrocity they all agreed to forget. As the fleet's fragile truce with the Vessh remnant expires, Ansel must reconstruct the massacre from fragments: corrupted logs, a survivor who may be lying, and her own suppressed memories of the night it happened. She discovers the records were rewritten by Fleet Command to protect an admiral whose experiment triggered the killings—and that her own testimony was edited out. In the end, Ansel broadcasts the true record in Vessh, forcing both species to hear it, at the cost of her immunity, her ship, and any hope of staying invisible; but in doing so she finally dreams in two languages at once, and finds that belonging means carrying witness rather than escaping it.
about_author: Yara Nystrom is a former shipping-log archivist who spent a decade cataloguing decommissioned vessel manifests before turning to fiction. She writes from a converted buoy-station office overlooking a harbor she insists is 'the closest thing to a launchpad I'll ever need.'

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Establishes her life aboard the freighter Pale Meridian's namesake route: silent ports, dead languages, and dreams she can't translate. Emotional beat: weary self-containment, the comfort of being no one.

chapters.title: A Name on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Ansel finds the impossible manifest listing the destroyed ship Meridian—with her buried birth name among the crew. POV: Ansel. Beat: cold dread; invisibility has failed.

chapters.title: Port of Small Lies
chapters.summary: At Ceres Anchorage, Ansel asks quiet questions and learns someone else has been asking about her. POV: Ansel. Beat: paranoia tightening like a harness.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Fleet broadcast announces the Vessh truce expires in ninety days. POV: interspersed fleet communiqués and Ansel. Beat: ticking pressure; history is about to repeat unless someone speaks.

chapters.title: Ilo Reyes
chapters.summary: A stranger boards at a fueling station claiming to be a Meridian survivor—officially, there are none. POV: alternating Ansel/Ilo. Beat: wary alliance born of mutual need.

chapters.title: What the Records Say
chapters.summary: Ansel pulls archived data: the Meridian never flew, no massacre occurred, no one named Okafor served. POV: Ansel. Beat: gaslit vertigo—reality itself feels edited.

chapters.title: Dreams in Vessh
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Ansel's linguistic training and the first night she dreamed in an alien tongue. POV: past-Ansel. Beat: tenderness curdling into foreboding.

chapters.title: Admiral Serevan
chapters.summary: Introduction of Admiral Serevan, architect of the truce and hero of the official record, giving a commemorative address. POV: Serevan. Beat: polished charisma over something rotten.

chapters.title: The Survivor's Version
chapters.summary: Ilo tells his account of the Meridian's final hours—but details contradict the physical evidence Ansel knows firsthand. POV: Ilo. Beat: doubt—is he witness or weapon?

chapters.title: Calyx Station
chapters.summary: They reach the derelict where the massacre occurred, hull scars matching no recorded battle. POV: Ansel. Beat: awe and grief; the silence here is load-bearing.

chapters.title: Ghost Signals
chapters.summary: Ansel recovers fragmented audio from the wreck—in Vessh voices, screaming, then her own younger voice. POV: Ansel. Beat: horror of hearing yourself in a crime you can't remember.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Mara Quist, Ansel's old training director, intercepts them with a warning and an offer: disappear again, safely. POV: Mara. Beat: seductive mercy—the price is complicity.

chapters.title: Ninety Minus Sixty
chapters.summary: Halfway point. The truce negotiations stall publicly; anti-Vessh riots begin on inner colonies. POV: news montage + Ansel. Beat: the world tilting toward repetition.

chapters.title: What Ilo Isn't Saying
chapters.summary: Ansel catches Ilo transmitting encrypted reports. Confrontation reveals he works for a faction inside Fleet Intelligence—not Serevan's. POV: Ilo. Beat: betrayal reframed as desperate hope.

chapters.title: The Experiment
chapters.summary: Decrypted files reveal Project Chorus: Serevan's attempt to weaponize Vessh language-cognition aboard the Meridian. POV: Ansel. Beat: sickening clarity—the massacre was a cover-up of a failure.

chapters.title: My Name in the File
chapters.summary: Ansel discovers her own testimony in the original logs—redacted, her identity erased. She was there. POV: Ansel. Beat: identity shatters; she is evidence.

chapters.title: Quist's Leash
chapters.summary: Mara reveals Ansel's memory was chemically sealed as part of the cover-up—and offers the counteragent. POV: Mara/Ansel. Beat: fear of what remembering will cost.

chapters.title: Remembering Calyx
chapters.summary: Under the counteragent, Ansel relives the massacre: Serevan's order, the Vessh crew begging in a language only she understood, her refusal translated into compliance. POV: Ansel (immersive). Beat: devastating guilt—the heart of the book.

chapters.title: The Language of Complicity
chapters.summary: Ansel understands why she stopped dreaming in human languages: her mind chose exile over bearing what she did. POV: Ansel. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Serevan's Summons
chapters.summary: Serevan invites Ansel aboard his flagship—an honor, a threat. Their conversation is a duel conducted entirely in courtesy. POV: alternating. Beat: chess across a table.

chapters.title: Terms of Silence
chapters.summary: Serevan offers restoration of her name, rank, and erased years—if she certifies the false record before the truce expires. POV: Ansel. Beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: Ilo's Gamble
chapters.summary: Ilo's faction plans to seize the archive by force; Ansel realizes force will trigger the war everyone fears. POV: Ilo. Beat: allies diverging.

chapters.title: The Vessh Remnant
chapters.summary: Against advice, Ansel opens a channel to the surviving Vessh chorus-fleet using the language she dreams in. POV: Ansel. Beat: terror and homecoming—they remember her voice.

chapters.title: What They Kept
chapters.summary: The Vessh reveal they preserved the true record all along, waiting for a human willing to carry it. POV: Vessh chorus / Ansel. Beat: belonging offered from the least expected place.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: With a month left, Ansel drafts the broadcast that could prevent war or start it. POV: Ansel. Beat: quiet dread before the storm.

chapters.title: Quist's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara must decide between protecting Ansel and protecting the institution that made them both. POV: Mara. Beat: tragic loyalty.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Anchor
chapters.summary: Serevan's agents board the Pale Meridian; Ilo is taken, the recovered logs seized. Ansel escapes with only the Vessh copy. POV: Ansel. Beat: everything lost but the truth.

chapters.title: Alone With It
chapters.summary: Hiding in the Calyx debris field, Ansel confronts whether truth without power is just another way to die. POV: Ansel. Beat: dark night of the soul.

chapters.title: The Chorus Decides
chapters.summary: The Vessh offer their fleet as escort for her broadcast—an act that will look like invasion if she fails. POV: Ansel/Vessh. Beat: trust as a wager.

chapters.title: Quist Defects
chapters.summary: Mara delivers the authentication keys stolen from Fleet archives, knowing it ends her career—or her life. POV: Mara. Beat: redemption purchased at full price.

chapters.title: Truce Eve
chapters.summary: Final day. Fleets mass at Calyx. Serevan prepares to declare the Vessh in violation. POV: multiple. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ansel transmits the unredacted record simultaneously in human and Vessh languages across every open channel. POV: Ansel. Beat: climax—one voice against an armada.

chapters.title: Serevan's Reply
chapters.summary: Serevan attempts to jam the signal and brand Ansel a Vessh asset; crews across both fleets begin refusing orders. POV: Serevan/Ansel. Beat: power meeting its limit.

chapters.title: The Mutiny of Listeners
chapters.summary: Ships on both sides hold position, listening. A young Vessh pilot and a human gunner refuse fire in mirrored acts. POV: ensemble. Beat: the tide turning through ordinary courage.

chapters.title: Fall of the Architect
chapters.summary: Confronted by his own officers with the authenticated logs, Serevan's command collapses; he invokes emergency powers no one honors. POV: Serevan. Beat: corruption devouring itself.

chapters.title: Ceasefire in Two Languages
chapters.summary: The truce is renegotiated with the true record as its foundation—fragile, honest, unprecedented. POV: Ansel. Beat: exhausted, cautious hope.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ansel gives formal testimony, reclaiming her name and accepting responsibility for her role under Chorus. POV: Ansel. Beat: accountability as liberation.

chapters.title: The Price Paid
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Ilo's fate revealed, Mara's sentence commuted to service, the Pale Meridian decommissioned. POV: ensemble. Beat: mourning what survival cost.

chapters.title: Dreaming Twice
chapters.summary: Ansel, aboard a new vessel on a new route, finally dreams in both languages at once—and understands both. POV: Ansel. Beat: integration; the wound becomes fluency.

chapters.title: Odile and the Orbit Revisited
chapters.summary: Closing chapter: Ansel visits the rebuilt Calyx memorial, where both species' names are read aloud each year—including hers. She stays visible. POV: Ansel. Beat: belonging chosen, not granted; the orbit completes.
